column1: # Quartermaster lifecycle-hook catalogue. Every row was checked on 2026-11-07 against the decompiled retail Lua in docs/mercs2-luacd/src/ (vz master = vz/xQ!L.lua, INFO name vz).

# Engine by-name call sites come from tools/wad_simulator/crates/mercs2_workshop/data/engine_lua_calls.tsv on branch feat/missions-lua-debugger (sha256 add4726eaf6030326eee45019148d7ed127079179e6d09a75fd5bda059b0fd68). "(computed)" there means the engine computes the module at call time. Module hashes were checked with tools/pandemic_hash.py --m2.
# Columns (tab-separated, no empty field; "-" = not applicable):
#   id       hook id passed to _G._QM.on(id, fn).
#   session  gameplay (world VM), front_end (shell VM) or both.
#   kind     splice = the hook IS the run of qm's own code spliced onto the end of host: it fires when the engine runs host's chunk. The loaders' entry points.
#            wrap  = qm splices compiled Lua onto the end of the module named in host. The splice runs after that module's top level and replaces the module global named in target with a wrapper.
#            event = subscribe to the retail script event whose exact Event.Post name is target.
#            state = subscribe to the game-state broadcast (Event.GameStateChange) for state target; the action (enter/exit) is the last part of id.

#   host     INFO name of the module the generated code is spliced onto. For wrap, that is the module that defines target. For event/state, it is the module the subscription lives in (vz for gameplay).
#            vz is the master script. A custom level runs its own master L instead (LoadLevel(L, L), levelbootstrap.lua:5-15), so in a level qm puts every vz row onto L.

#            A wrap's target must be a function the host's main chunk defines in the bytecode qm splices onto (mercs2_formats::script_meta::main_run(..).functions); one it does not define fails the link, naming the hook and the host.
#            mrxsound, mrxguishell and mrxguiattractmode exist byte-identical in shell/ and resident/; session picks the block (front_end = shell block copy).
#   target   wrap: the global function as the module defines it. event: the Event.Post name. state: the state name as retail spells it.
#   call     before = dispatch, then call the original; after = call the original, then dispatch; "-" for event/state.
#            Rule: before when the hook marks an ending (exit, close, end, cleanup, teardown, hand-off) or the original destroys what a handler reads. after otherwise.

#            The filter column is the "dispatch only when ..." of fires, as the wrapper evaluates it. Anything it reads must be read before calling the original, and the original's return value is always passed through.
#            Rows that share a (host, target) pair are ONE wrapper with a filter per id; generate one wrapper per pair, never one per id. The pairs are:
#              world.begin + world.retry; contract.retry + contract.dismiss; job.completed + mission.completed (MrxTask.Complete).

#   filter   "-", or when the hook dispatches: "args: <Lua expression>" is evaluated over the call's arguments (...) before the original runs; "results: <Lua expression>" over the original's return values (...) after it. The expression runs in the host's env, so it reads the host's globals.

#   evidence first docs/... token = definition (wrap: "function <target>(" at column 0; event: the Event.Post line; state: a retail subscription line). Then the fire sites, and any engine by-name rows (pc-v10 / pc-v11 call-site VAs).
